correctness.rationale: For each interior point, the normal foot on an edge is internal exactly when its signed edge projection lies strictly between endpoint values; vertex support normals correspond to positive dot products with both incident edge rays. In an obtuse triangle at apex A, the two acute vertices and BC always contribute three bases; signs of x·u and x·v cannot both be negative since x=s u+t v for s,t>0. Exactly two positives yield 6 total normals, exactly one yields 4. Intersections of the two altitude boundaries with opposite side give z_low=-g/(V-g), z_high=U/(U-g), hence the 6-normal area fraction (UV-g²)/((U-g)(V-g)); the rest have four. For fixed angle t=-cos(theta) and ratio r, the rational p expression and nonnegative square-gap identity prove the unique isosceles maximum and nonattained infimum 0. Independently checked representative exact rational chamber fractions and 507 rational interior sample counts; proof applies to continuous area measure, excluding null bifurcation lines.
